findings.title: ADR-0008 Q5 claims 'full v1 scope' wrapper unwrapping (sudo, env, time, nice, timeout, xargs, command, bash -c/sh -c, $()) but v1 never had this code
findings.claim: r3 decisions: 'Q5 full v1 scope: the parser unwraps sudo, env, time, nice, timeout, xargs, command, bash -c/sh -c strings and $( )/backticks before it reads argv0.'

archaeology.introduced_by: NONE FOUND. git log -S for 'sudo', 'xargs', 'timeout', 'nice', 'bash -c' against hooks/core/routing.mjs returns zero commits across all 2230 commits of v1 history. 'env' and 'command ' only appear in unrelated commits (dcab56fd #817 size threshold, f8d23289 #463/#470 heredoc routing) that do not add wrapper unwrapping.
archaeology.original_intent: v1's curl/wget detection (routing.mjs:735-765, verified present) operates on shell segments split by && || ; and a regex test for curl/wget at word boundaries. There is no wrapper-command (sudo/xargs/timeout/nice/bash -c) unwrapping logic anywhere in the 1017-line file's history.
archaeology.regression_risk: ADR-0008 frames this as restoring/matching v1 behavior ('v1'deki gibi olsun', owner decision: hard deny with v1 scope and its issues fixed). Wrapper unwrapping for sudo/env/time/nice/timeout/xargs/command/bash -c is NEW parser surface, not a v1 fix. Calling it 'full v1 scope' is a factual misstatement that will mislead reviewers into assuming this path is battle-tested against the 2230-commit issue history. It is not: there is no issue number cited for sudo/xargs/timeout/nice unwrapping in the fixes table (# column), unlike every other row in ADR-0008's change table which cites issue numbers.
archaeology.safe_fix_constraints: Either (a) relabel Q5 as new/untested scope rather than 'full v1 scope', and add explicit golden cases (GP3) for sudo/xargs/timeout/nice/bash -c wrapping curl+stdout, or (b) if the owner truly wants hard-deny-with-v1-scope-only, drop the wrapper unwrapping beyond what v1 had ($( ) backtick and env were effectively absent too) and treat it as a separate, flagged enhancement.

findings.fix: Correct the ADR-0008 Q5 text to state this is new parser coverage (not v1 parity), and add golden cases for each wrapper (sudo curl ... | stdout, xargs -I{} curl, timeout 5 curl, nice curl, bash -c 'curl ...') to GP3 so the new grammar is actually exercised before release.

findings.title: ADR-0016 case B/C 'same selection as ADR-0009' claim is not shown to be literally the same algorithm — different score weights, same budgeted-greedy shape
findings.claim: 'No case cuts text: the wrapper and the replacement select whole chunks by BM25 score against the intent, under a byte budget (budgeted greedy, the same selection as ADR-0009).'

archaeology.method: doc comparison: docs/v2/adr/0009-compaction-and-memory.md section 4 vs docs/v2/adr/0016-subagent-context-protection.md 'Three cases' table
archaeology.introduced_by: doc-only (ADR-0016, ADR-0009), no code yet — not a v1 regression
archaeology.original_intent: ADR-0009's budgeted greedy selects over journal ROWS scored by (open-error/prompt/edit/index weight) x recency-decay x repeat-bonus, with a decaying per-section ratio (0.7^k) to keep sections mixed, and an explicit 640B cutoff for pointer-ification. ADR-0016's chunk selection scores by BM25 against a free-text 'intent' string over arbitrary tool output, with no sections, no recency decay, no 0.7^k mixing term.
archaeology.regression_risk: These are two different scoring functions (integer recency/importance score vs BM25 relevance score) that happen to share the 'take by ratio, skip what doesn't fit, never cut mid-item' greedy shape. Calling them 'the same selection' overstates shared implementation and risks one being changed without updating the other, or a reviewer skipping verification of ADR-0016's selection assuming ADR-0009's golden cases (GP6) already cover it. They do not: GP6 cases are all about the 2048B session-state block, not about BM25 chunk selection under the 16384B OUTPUT_CAP.
archaeology.safe_fix_constraints: Keep the greedy/no-truncation invariant shared, but document the two scoring functions as distinct, and add GP3 golden cases that specifically test ADR-0016's BM25-against-intent selection (e.g., multiple chunks where highest BM25 chunk is the last one yielded by a command, confirm it is the chunk returned, and confirm 'more:' pointer appears when the full output exceeds OUTPUT_CAP).

findings.fix: Rename ADR-0016's claim to 'the same greedy-by-ratio, never-truncate shape as ADR-0009' (not 'the same selection'), and add BM25-specific golden cases distinct from ADR-0009's GP6.

findings.title: ADR-0008 GP3 golden cases omit wrapper-unwrap cases entirely
findings.claim: Golden cases (GP3) table lists 11 cases, none involving sudo/xargs/timeout/nice/bash -c/env wrapping a curl/HTTP call, despite Q5 naming all of these as in-scope for the parser.

archaeology.regression_risk: Untested grammar branches (sudo, xargs, timeout, nice, bash -c, $()) are exactly the kind of surface where a new recursive-descent parser is likely to have edge cases (e.g. xargs -I{} curl {}, nested $(curl ...) inside another command substitution, bash -c with single vs double quoting of the inner string). Shipping without golden cases for these means the stated Q5 scope is unverified at release time.
archaeology.safe_fix_constraints: Add at least one golden case per wrapper type named in Q5 before the parser is marked done.

findings.fix: Extend GP3 with one row per wrapper type: sudo curl, env curl, time curl, nice curl, timeout N curl, xargs -I{} curl {}, command curl, bash -c 'curl ...', $(curl ...).
